## Court matters

- **Item:** The Public Protector found that tweets on colonialism made by Zille on 15 March 2017, while she was Western Cape premier, breached the Executive Ethics Code and the Constitution, and recommended remedial action (Report No. 5 of 2018/19). Zille's review application was dismissed by the Gauteng Division of the High Court, Pretoria, and she appealed. · `Disputed` — [source](https://lawlibrary.org.za/akn/za/judgment/zasca/2022/16/eng@2022-02-07), 2022-02-07 (retrieved 2026-11-15, time not logged); also [source](https://www.supremecourtofappeal.org.za/images/Media_Summaries_2022/sca2022-16ms.pdf), 2022-02-07; also [source](https://www.citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/courts/sca-rules-against-mkhwebane-zille-colonialism-tweets/), 2022-02-07
  - **Status / outcome:** The SCA upheld the appeal and reviewed and set aside the Public Protector's findings and remedial action (Report No. 5 of 2018/19), 7 Feb 2022 (Premier of the Western Cape Province v The Public Protector & Another (771/2020) [2022] ZASCA 16). (matter_status: `cleared`)
